Hi f4nt4,

I'd really like to help you get this sorted out. To better understand what's going on with your system, could you help me out with some details?

About your system: What version of Windows are you running, and is everything up to date? Also, have you updated your BIOS recently, and if so, do you know which version you're currently on?

The graphics driver 8735 is an intel driver, have you tried using 

HP Graphics Drivers

https://support.hp.com/in-en/drivers/hp-omnibook-ultra-flip-14-inch-2-in-1-laptop-next-gen-ai-pc-14-fh0000/2102254404

? And when you mention crashes - does this happen with other GPU-intensive tasks like games or benchmarks, or just with your AI workloads?

Regarding your llama.cpp setup: What kind of models are you running (size, settings, etc.), and how much GPU memory does it typically use before things go sideways? Does it crash right away or only after you've been using it for a while? Are you using any custom settings or modifications?

Are you seeing any specific error messages? And have you tried other apps that use Vulkan or SYCL to see if it's just a llama.cpp that is crashing?

Best regards,

Hi Louie,

Thanks for reaching out to me! 🙂

Here the requested infos:

Windows: Win 11 25H2 - Build 26200.8246 (will try to update to 26H1 while you guys are sleeping 🤓)

BIOS: HP W75 Ver. 01.04.02, 09.12.2025 (latest HP is providing atm)

HP is providing 32.0.101.7026 Rev.B, which according to the Windows Device Manager, is the identical version I've downgrade to:

 

I've tried to reproduce the issue by running Furmark (v2.10.2 - latest version) and also the VRAM stresstest with OCCT (v16.1.9 - latest version). I additionally run the build-in RAM test of the HP BIOS and memtest86+ (v8.00).

Non of them triggered a crash or didn't found RAM related issues.

These are my llama.cpp settings:

llama-server.exe \
--port 5801 \
--threads 4 \
--no-mmap \
--mlock \
--parallel 1 \
--cache-type-k q8_0 \
--cache-type-v q8_0 \
--model w:\llm\unsloth_gemma-4-E2B-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
--mmproj W:\llm\gemma-4-E2B\mmproj-BF16.gguf \
-ngl 999 \
--ctx-size 3000 \
-ub 512 \
--reasoning off \
--reasoning-budget 0 \
--cache-ram 0 \
--n-predict 2048 \
--no-cache-prompt


So basically Gemma4 - E2B in a low quantized version, which is not really (v)RAM heavy with these settings, but I've tried many settings.

Also tried different RAM <-> vRAM allocation through the Intel Graphics Software, but also didn't helped.

On driver version 8626, llama.cpp crashes every few inferencing tasks. Sometimes sooner, sometimes later.

On 8735 the screen becomes right away black, with a visible mouse cursor, but Windows is right away not responsible anymore and needs to be hard rebooted by holding the Power button for 5+ seconds.

It's regardless if it's a basic prompt like "write a 1000 word story" or something like audio transcription.

Memory consumption only goes up during model loading (~5GB) and a bit (~200MB) while prompt processing or inferencing. Again, nothing really (v)RAM heavy.

I haven't tested any other tools besides llama.cpp, but could try LM studio. But as LM studio is using the llama.cpp egine, I'm expecting the same result.

I sadly don't see any error message before the crashes. Neither through the debug logs of llama.cpp or within the Windows Event log, but I'm happy to take suggestions on how to get proper logs in such cases 🙂

Hope this helps for the beginning!

Best
